To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an unsu- pervised domain adaptation framework to estimate CTR based on adversarial neural networks and that our system achieves state of the art results in the domain adaptation task.
we have designed a novel framework for unsupervised domain adaptive segmentation of chest organs, which is able to accurately estimate the CTR in CXRs.

(i) We propose an unsupervized domain adaptation method based on adversarial learning for the automatic estimation of CTR, (ii) We show that our method can achieve state of the art performance on the publicly available JSRT dataset, (iii) We demonstrate that our method is clinically useful for the diagnosis of cardio megaly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an automatic system to estimate cardiothoracic ratios from CXRs.
the automatic estimation of CTR from CXRs and the proposed unsupervised domain adaption framework is a first step towards this goal.
the development of a system to assist clinicians in the estimation of CTR in CXRs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is able to learn from a source dataset and transfer the learned knowledge to a target dataset.
our system is a promising tool to assist clinicians in the process of diagnosis of cardiomegalia.
we have developed a system that is clinically relevant and can assist clinicians in the process of diagnosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are the first to introduce a model that learns domain invariant features from openly available data for the task of chest organ segmentation, and demonstrate the clinical usefulness of such a model.
our system is the first to perform CTR estimation in an unsupervised fashion.
our model can produce accurate segmentation results without the need of any pixel level annotation and thus can be used for the estimation of CTR in CXRs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show how to use openly available data for domain adaptation in the medical imaging domain.
we demonstrate the potential of domain adaptation techniques for medical image analysis.
domain adaptation techniques can be successfully applied to the problem of automatic CTR estimation.
